claims.text: Heat treatment can induce measurable short-range-order changes in HfNbTiVAl10.
The heat-treated HfNbTiVAl10 has controlled, defined interfacial defect densities.
Atom probe tomography can quantify short-range order.
Atom probe tomography can provide the proposed clustering, domain-size, and interfacial-defect-density SRO descriptors in HfNbTiVAl10.
Digital image correlation or in situ diffraction can supply descriptors of transient heterostructural evolution, including phase-transformation indicators or evolving defect statistics.
Regression models such as Gaussian-process and random-forest regressors can be trained using numerical features to predict mechanical-property targets.
Combined SRO and dynamic microstructural descriptors can predict Young's modulus in HfNbTiVAl10.
Combined SRO and dynamic microstructural descriptors can predict yield strength in HfNbTiVAl10.
Combined SRO and dynamic microstructural descriptors can predict fracture behavior or fracture toughness in HfNbTiVAl10.
The SRO features of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 govern dislocation motion.
The SRO features of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 govern crack nucleation.
A machine-learning surrogate can bypass complicated, time-consuming physics-based calculations and make prediction easier or faster.
The proposed framework will reduce computational and experimental prediction time or computational burden by approximately 50%.
The proposed framework will improve prediction RMSE for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness by 20–30% relative to established simulations.
The combined SRO and dynamic descriptors will be strongly and statistically significantly correlated with mechanical response across the stated temperatures and strain rates.
Conventional full-scale atomistic and continuum simulations require more extensive computational resources and are less rapid than the proposed framework.
The model may fail when phase transformations or drastic heterostructural changes are not represented by the selected descriptors.
Independent split-Hopkinson-bar measurements can determine the stated tensile and fracture quantities while supplying the proposed SRO and dynamic descriptors.

contradictions.description: The intervention appropriately distinguishes static APT measurements from in situ monitoring, whereas the falsification design describes static SRO by APT as being measured simultaneously in situ during split-Hopkinson-bar testing. APT is a destructive post-test or separate-specimen method, so these descriptions are operationally inconsistent.
